subject: Enterprise Access Controls questionnaire — provisioning & SSO follow-up
messages:
From: Selena Cho <selena.cho@acme-inc.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme-inc.com
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Enterprise IAM questionnaire — follow-up items

Ben,

Thanks for sending the initial questionnaire last week. Our security team reviewed Redwood's responses and had a couple of follow-ups specifically related to provisioning cadence, group sync, and SSO assertion attributes. Key asks below so we can close our RFP: 

- Confirm SCIM API support for PATCH operations and bulkCreate/bulkReplace semantics. We need to provision ~50k users from our HR system during onboarding.
- Describe how group membership is synced (push vs. pull) and whether nested groups are supported.
- For SAML/OIDC: which attributes are available for mapping to RBAC (e.g., department, jobTitle, groups claim)? Do you support encrypted assertions?
- What audit trails exist for admin actions related to role assignments?

Could you reply with concrete API paths, example payloads, and any relevant metadata files? We prefer attachments or a short spec document.

Regards,
Selena Cho
Director, Security Ops
Acme Inc.
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Selena Cho <selena.cho@acme-inc.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 11:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Enterprise IAM questionnaire — follow-up items

Selena —

Appreciate the clear list. Below is a compact, actionable summary and I've attached two artifacts: a SCIM mapping PDF and our SAML metadata XML. If you want, we can schedule a short walkthrough.

SCIM provisioning
- SCIM v2.0 support (RFC 7643/7644).
- PATCH: supported (JSON Patch and PATCH with partial update). Endpoint: POST /scim/v2/Users/{id} (PATCH semantics accepted); also support PUT for full replace.
- Bulk operations: job-based bulk import for large initial syncs (bulkCreate/bulkReplace). We accept a CSV/NDJSON payload via a staging job endpoint: POST /scim/v2/bulk/jobs with job manifest. Typical throughput: 10k users/hour on a single dedicated pool; we provide import tooling for one-time onboarding.
- Attribute mapping: custom mapping layer in Redwood Console; default mappings include userName, externalId, name (given/family), email, department, title, manager, and custom attributes. See attached redwood_scim_mapping_v1.pdf for example mappings and JSON schema.

Groups and group sync
- Push model: SCIM Group resource support with POST/PUT/PATCH to /scim/v2/Groups. Works for group create, update, membership change.
- Nested groups: supported; we persist memberOf links and expose them in the Group.members array and delta tokens.
- Delta sync: incremental sync using startIndex + filter + 'If-None-Match' style tokens; also support checkpoint tokens for long-running syncs.

SSO (SAML & OIDC)
- SAML: metadata attachment included (redwood_saml_metadata.xml). We support signed and encrypted assertions. ACS endpoints: https://api.redwood.com/sso/saml/acs/{tenant}.
- OIDC: standard discovery document at https://auth.redwood.com/.well-known/openid-configuration; supports id_token claims mapping and SCIM-based provisioning for JIT provisioning flows.
- Attribute mapping: we can map SAML attributes or OIDC claims to role bindings and to user profile fields. Common attributes we recommend: email, groups, department, jobTitle, employeeId.
- JIT provision: supported for both SAML and OIDC — you can create accounts on first login with configurable default role mapping.

RBAC and admin controls
- Role model: pre-defined roles (Super Admin, Org Admin, Security Admin, Developer, Read-only) plus custom roles with fine-grained permissions (API keys, model deployment, billing, audit).
- Group-based role assignment: map IdP groups to Redwood roles. Nested group resolution is applied when evaluating role membership.
- Admin audit logs: immutable audit trail for role change events, SSO logins, API key creation, and SCIM jobs. Logs are retained by default 365 days (configurable up to 7 years for enterprise contracts) and available via Console and an exportable JSONL endpoint.

Security & compliance notes
- TLS 1.2+ for all endpoints, support for customer KMS for token encryption in Private deployments.
- MFA: Redwood supports enforcing MFA at login via IdP (recommended) and can require platform-level MFA for specific admin roles.

Next steps
- I attached the SCIM mapping PDF and SAML metadata. If you need sample PATCH and bulk job payloads, I can drop those as separate attachments or walk through them on a call. Would Thursday 11/13 at 10:00 PT work for a 30-minute walkthrough?

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

Ben —

Thanks, that's very helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side before we confirm the walkthrough: 

1) For bulk onboarding: when you say "10k users/hour on a single dedicated pool" — can you provide guidance on how throughput scales with more pools or higher concurrency? We want to estimate onboarding duration for 50k users plus 5k groups.
2) For encrypted SAML assertions: do you support AES-256 encryption and which key management options are available (customer-managed keys vs. Redwood-managed)?
3) For audit exports: can we pull incremental audit events via an API? We prefer to ship logs to our SIEM in near real-time.

Also, attached is our current MFA and provisioning requirement spreadsheet (acme_mfa_requirements.xlsx) with a few fields you might use to validate compatibility.

Selena
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Selena Cho <selena.cho@acme-inc.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 16 Nov 2025 16:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Enterprise IAM questionnaire — follow-up items

Selena — quick answers inline, and see the attached short spec and a Drive folder with sample payloads. If helpful, Tessa can run numbers for throughput based on the Dedicated pool sizes you expect.

1) Throughput scaling for bulk onboarding:
- Baseline: single dedicated pool (NVIDIA-A100 class) ~10k users/hour during import, depending on profile complexity and attribute transforms.
- Horizontal scaling: additional dedicated instances linearly increase job throughput; typically each additional pool adds ~8k-12k users/hour depending on concurrent network IO and transform work. For 50k users + 5k groups, a safe planning guideline is 3 pools (estimate ~28k-36k users/hour combined) to complete in under 2 hours for user creation and group attachments — however, we recommend scheduling off-peak and using our staging manifest to parallelize across pools.

2) Encrypted SAML assertions & KMS:
- We support encrypted assertions with AES-256 (XML Encryption). Keys can be customer-managed via KMS/HSM integrations in Private deployments; in hosted mode, we support customer key rotation via an encrypted key store and rotation API. We provide key import for SAML decryption keys if you prefer to manage credentials.

3) Audit exports / SIEM integration:
- Yes: incremental audit export API available: GET /audit/events?since=<iso_timestamp>&limit=1000 returns event batches. We also support streaming audit events to a customer-owned Kafka endpoint or pushing to an HTTPS webhook (with retry/backpressure). Typical delivery is near real-time (<10s) for critical admin events.

Attachments provided:
- redwood_scim_mapping_v1.pdf (SCIM mapping examples and attribute table)
- redwood_saml_metadata.xml (SAML endpoints & certs)
- Drive folder with sample PATCH and bulk job payloads: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cScimDocs

If that looks good I propose the walkthrough on Monday 11/17 at 09:00 PT so Tessa can run a quick sizing estimate with exact pool counts. If you prefer Thursday 11/13 as earlier suggested, we can do that too — I realize calendar got tight.

Best,
Ben
